description: Twelve historical reference points. A registry of locations and evidence only: not a list of landing sites, and no condition is pre-evaluated.

coordinateSource.title: NSSDCA Lunar Artifact Impacts and Landing Sites list
coordinateSource.frame: DE421 mean Earth/polar axis reference frame
coordinateSource.precisionStatement: Precision of knowledge of location is reflected in the precision of the coordinates (0.001 degrees is approximately 30 m).

terrainProducts.name: LOLA GDR LDEM_4 (shipped with the app, converted to int16)
terrainProducts.versionNote: The converted JSON records only the source name; the PDS product version at conversion time was not recorded.
terrainProducts.format: Project int16 grid (metres above a 1737.4 km sphere); source is PDS3 float IMG
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: 4 pixels/degree, about 7.6 km at the equator
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: Not stated; slopes are strongly smoothed.
terrainProducts.frame: Not recorded in the converted file (source: DE421 mean Earth/polar axis)
terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height above a 1737.4 km reference sphere
limitations: Regional background only.

terrainProducts.name: LOLA GDR LDEM_512 tiles
terrainProducts.versionNote: PRODUCT_CREATION_TIME 2017-09-15 in the label of LDEM_512_00N_45N_000_090_FLOAT.
terrainProducts.format: PDS3 IMG, PC_REAL float32, kilometres relative to 1737.4 km; one 45-degree latitude band per tile
terrainProducts.coverage: Global (16 tiles listed in the directory)
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: Label: surface-fitting (GMT surface) compensates for incomplete coverage, so effective resolution is coarser than the grid between laser tracks. Not quantified.
terrainProducts.frame: Mean Earth/polar axis of DE421 (label COORDINATE_SYSTEM_NAME)
terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height relative to a 1737.4 km reference sphere

availability.note: Plain HTTP; labels read. Browser cross-origin access not tested; tiles are about 4 GB each.

limitations: Interpolated between tracks.

terrainProducts.name: LOLA GDR LDEM_60S_60M
terrainProducts.format: PDS3 IMG, PC_REAL float32, kilometres relative to 1737.4 km; polar stereographic, true scale at the pole
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: Label: ground tracks are interpolated (GMT blockmedian and surface). Effective resolution not quantified.
terrainProducts.frame: Mean Earth/polar axis of DE421; planetocentric
terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height relative to a 1737.4 km reference sphere

availability.note: Plain HTTP; label read. File is about 3.9 GB.

limitations: Only the Chandrayaan-3 candidate lies inside this product.

terrainProducts.name: SLDEM2015 (LOLA + SELENE Terrain Camera)
terrainProducts.publisher: NASA PDS Geosciences Node / LOLA team
terrainProducts.format: PDS3 IMG, PC_REAL float32, kilometres relative to 1737.4 km (also JP2)
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: PGDA describes the Terrain Camera source as about 60-100 m effective horizontal resolution (agent-reported, not re-read).

verticalAccuracy.note: Barker et al. report a typical vertical accuracy of about 3-4 m (agent-reported abstract, statistic not stated). The 1-degree data-quality map gives RMS LOLA-TC residuals per cell, read for the candidates in this catalogue.

terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height relative to a 1737.4 km reference sphere
terrainProducts.qualityInformation: sldem2015_data_quality_float: 1 pixel/degree map of RMS vertical residual between unbinned LOLA data and the co-registered TC tile (metres)

availability.note: Plain HTTP; tile label and quality map read.

limitations: Does not cover the Chandrayaan-3 candidate (latitude beyond 60 degrees).

terrainProducts.name: SELENE TC SLDEM2013 (DTM_MAP)
terrainProducts.versionNote: PRODUCT_VERSION_ID "01" in the tile label read; data set SLN-L-TC-5-SLDEM2013-V1.0.
terrainProducts.format: PDS3 IMG, 16-bit MSB integer in metres (1 m quantisation); 1x1 degree tiles
terrainProducts.coverage: Global tiles down to the poles (agent-reported); Chandrayaan-3 tile label read
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: Label: bilinear resampling and SMOOTHING_WIDTH = 50, so the effective resolution is much coarser than 7.4 m. Not quantified. Source images are about 10 m/pixel (agent-reported).

verticalAccuracy.note: JAXA DARTS page: "nearly 10 meters or better" (agent-reported, statistic not stated).

terrainProducts.frame: Planetocentric, 1737.4 km sphere; mean Earth versus principal axis not stated
terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height above a 1737.4 km reference sphere
terrainProducts.qualityInformation: Label QA_PERCENT_* fields (good, dummy, bad, interpolated, shadow pixel percentages)

availability.note: Plain HTTP directory; one label read.

limitations: Frame relative to LOLA products not verified.

terrainProducts.name: LROC NAC DTMs
terrainProducts.versionNote: Version differs per DTM (dtm_vers field, recorded per DTM in each candidate).
terrainProducts.publisher: LROC / Arizona State University, archived in the PDS
terrainProducts.format: PDS IMG float32 (metres) with PDS3 header and PDS4 xml label; GeoTIFF; _CONF confidence map (uint8); orthophotos; README
terrainProducts.coverage: Individual footprints of a few to tens of km; 662 footprints in the catalogue released through 2026-09-15
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: 2, 3 or 5 m depending on the DTM
terrainProducts.effectiveResolutionNote: Product page: DTM resolution can be 3 to 10 times the image pixel scale. Relative precision is better than the DTM pixel scale (2 to 5 m) per Henriksen et al.

verticalAccuracy.note: Per DTM: relat_le, vertical precision at 90 % confidence calculated by SOCET SET. Absolute accuracy about 1 m vertical and about 10 m horizontal (Henriksen et al., abstract).

horizontalAccuracy.note: About 10 m horizontally relative to LOLA profiles (abstract); statistic not stated.

terrainProducts.frame: Registered to LOLA tracks; label gives a 1737.4 km sphere, planetocentric latitude, east positive; shapefile GCS name Moon_2000
terrainProducts.verticalDatum: Height above a 1737.4 km reference sphere
terrainProducts.qualityInformation: Confidence map. The README table (read only for APOLLO11) is: 0 no data, 1 shadowed, 2 saturated, 3 suspicious, 4 interpolated or extrapolated, 10-14 successful correlation, 15 manually edited. Whether every DTM uses the same table was not confirmed; several DTMs show codes outside it.

availability.note: Plain HTTP with range requests. The old pds.lroc.im-ldi.com path redirects to pds.mcp.nasa.gov, which has no directory listing. Browser cross-origin access not tested.

limitations: Known artifacts per README: boxes, seams, faceted areas, noise.

In the labels read, upperleft_corner_x has the opposite sign to the usual convention and the Chandrayaan-3 polar stereographic origin latitude is a latitude of true scale; both were verified against the label bounding coordinates for those products only.

terrainProducts.name: Chang'e-2 CCD global DEM (CE2TMap2015)
terrainProducts.coverage: Global according to the producer; tiles for these points not checked
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: 20 m and 50 m DEMs (sources disagree on whether a 7 m DEM exists)

verticalAccuracy.note: A comparison paper reports 2.3 m mean vertical difference against SLDEM2015 with 183 m horizontal inconsistency (agent-reported snippet).

terrainProducts.frame: GCS_Moon_2000 sphere; axis system not stated

availability.note: Registration is required according to the research agent; the catalogue could not be browsed (JavaScript portal).

limitations: Not used.

terrainProducts.name: Chang'e 3/4/5 descent-camera or rover DEMs
terrainProducts.publisher: NAOC / BACC / CNSA (papers by Liu, Di, Bo et al.)
terrainProducts.coverage: About 1-2 km around the landing sites (CE-5) and tens to hundreds of metres (CE-4), per papers
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: Reported 0.02-0.4 m depending on the product

verticalAccuracy.note: Not stated in the papers read by the research agent.

availability.note: No data-availability statement or download found. This is not evidence that the data do not exist or cannot be requested.

limitations: Not usable by the app.

terrainProducts.name: Chandrayaan-2 OHRC DEMs (ISRO/SAC)
terrainProducts.coverage: Eight candidate sites including the primary Chandrayaan-3 site LS-2 (4 km x 2.4 km)
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: LPSC 2023 abstract: "DEM at 0.32m grid interval having a height resolution of 0.05m" (read from the PDF text); height resolution is not a vertical accuracy.

availability.note: The PRADAN Chandrayaan-2 page lists imagery but no DEM product (agent-reported); downloads require login. Not evidence that the data cannot be requested.

limitations: Even at 0.32 m posting, 0.3 m obstacles could at best be flagged, not excluded.

terrainProducts.name: Independent OHRC-derived DEM at the Chandrayaan-3 site
terrainProducts.format: Announced; the Zenodo record contained only a PDF when checked

verticalAccuracy.note: Preprint reports an estimated relative vertical precision of 40-50 cm and NMAD 2.88 m against the NAC DEM; not independently verified.

horizontalAccuracy.note: Lander about 30 m from ISRO coordinates after tie-point alignment (preprint).

terrainProducts.frame: Oblique stereographic on a 1737.4 km sphere

availability.note: Authors state products will be archived with a DOI upon acceptance.

limitations: Re-evaluate if released.

terrainProducts.name: Chandrayaan-2 TMC-2 DTM
terrainProducts.coverage: Tile covering the candidate not confirmed
terrainProducts.gridSpacingNote: Imagery is about 5 m; DTM grid not found.

availability.note: Login required according to the research agent; a USGS description page returned HTTP 403.

limitations: Low priority.

terrainProducts.name: High-Resolution LOLA Topography for Lunar South Pole Sites
terrainProducts.versionNote: No version number; dated updates 2021-04-26 to 2022-08-15 listed on the page.
terrainProducts.coverage: Named south-polar sites; the page gives no latitude bounds, so coverage of -69.37 is not confirmed (first 100,000 characters of the page read)

verticalAccuracy.note: Page: median RMS height error about 0.30-0.50 m; median RMS slope error about 1.5-2.5 degrees (statistic definitions not read).

availability.note: Page reachable; ROI shapefiles or README not checked for coordinate extents.

limitations: Coverage of the Chandrayaan-3 candidate unverified; it is probably outside the named sites (inference).

terrainProducts.name: Moon Trek WMTS image tiles

availability.note: Documented in the requirements as image tiles; not opened in this step.

limitations: Tiles are not numeric DEMs and must not be used for calculations.

candidates.name: Apollo 11 LM descent stage

alternateCoordinates.coordinateMethod: Averaged Mapping Orbit NACs + Laser Ranging
alternateCoordinates.frame: IAU Moon 2000 geographic coordinate system (shapefile README); frame equivalence with the NSSDCA DE421 mean Earth/polar axis frame not verified

hardware.description: Descent stage of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module "Eagle". The catalogued coordinate marks the hardware itself.
hardware.dimensionsNote: Octagonal prism 4.2 m across and 1.7 m thick; footpad ends on opposite legs 9.4 m apart; legs hold the stage bottom 1.5 m above the surface (NSSDCA 1969-059C).

footprintOverlap.basis: The coordinate is the centre of the descent stage (NSSDCA, LROC). A footprint of radius 1.5 m centred on it overlaps a stage of about 2.1 m half-width whenever the offset is below about 3.6 m; the LROC uncertainty (0.3 m) is smaller than that. Derived by geometry; the footprint has not been registered against orthophotos.

coverage.note: Global product; tile directory listed and one tile label read. The tile containing this point was not opened.
Label states latitudes within +/-60 degrees; point is inside.

regionalProducts.qualityResidualNote: RMS vertical residual between LOLA altimetry and the co-registered TC tile in the 1-degree cell containing the point (SLDEM2015 data-quality map).

coverage.note: Tile for this point not opened.
Point lies inside the published footprint polygon and a DTM value exists at the point pixel.

limitations: Catalogue registration only: no terrain, power or communication condition has been evaluated for this point.
A successful point sample of a DTM shows that data exist at one pixel; it does not validate the 3 m footprint or the surrounding terrain.
